name: William W. Phelps
role: Church printer and editor in Missouri
dateNote: He was baptized on 16 June 1831, two days after section 55, and was named Church printer in July 1831.
importance: William W. Phelps was a newspaper editor from Canandaigua, New York. Section 55 calls him to be baptized and to help Oliver Cowdery with printing and school books. Section 57 plants him at Independence as Church printer, where a mob destroyed his press on 20 July 1833. He helped compile the 1835 D&C and its hymnal; he was excommunicated in 1838 and 1839 and rebaptized in 1840.
connections: He works with Oliver Cowdery, John Whitmer, and Martin Harris on the revelations, and served as counselor to David Whitmer in Missouri.

sources.title: William Wines Phelps, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Dates, offices, press destruction, excommunications and 1840 rebaptism checked on JSP. Bare “William” (55:1) left out as ambiguous. His role presenting section 134 comes from the 134 study file.
